To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the relationship between teacher and student performance is positive in both reading and mathematics, and stronger in reading than in mathematics.

1) the relationship between teacher performance and student achievement is strong and positive in reading, but not in mathematics; 2) teacher evaluation scores are positively related to student achievement in reading when used as a predictor of student performance; and 3) the relationship between reading teacher performance and student reading achievement is stronger than the relationship between mathematics teacher performance and student mathematics achievement because of differences in the knowledge and alignment of teachers and evaluators in reading and mathematics.

teacher evaluation scores were positively and significantly related to reading achievement, positively related, but not significant, to math achievement, and positively and significantly related when inserted as a predictor of student achievement.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the validity and utility of a teacher evaluation system in a high stakes knowledge and skills based teacher pay system.
the validity of a new, performance based teacher evaluation system.
the validity of a teacher evaluation system, which has been used to inform teacher and administrator pay decisions in a large urban school district.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the relationship between teacher and student performance is stronger in reading and weaker in math, which is a reflection of both the teachers and the evaluators' knowledge and alignment.
the teacher evaluation system is a valid measure of student achievement in reading, but it is a less valid measure in mathematics.
the relationship between teacher and student achievement is positive but weak.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have found evidence for the validity of the teacher evaluation system in the context of the knowledge and skills based compensation system.
the relationship between teacher evaluations and student achievement is stronger in reading, which is a result of both teacher and evaluator knowledge of reading instruction and assessment.
teacher evaluation scores are related to student achievement in reading, but not in mathematics.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a performance based evaluation system is not a substitute for professional development.
a performance-based evaluation system that is aligned to the curriculum, standards, and assessments is a valid and reliable way to evaluate teacher performance.

teacher evaluation scores can be a valid measure of student achievement when the evaluation system is designed to align with standards, assessments, and the pedagogical knowledge of teachers and evaluators.
